title: AI Game Wishlist
author: RamonDozol
selftext:
This is a post where the people without access to the skills, hardware or Best AI can share their desires and ideas for games they would love to play/test, with the intent that maybe someone else is already working on something that they would like, or might like the idea and start developing it.   


Basicaly, its a wishlist for AI Games that people can ask the AI Devs to make.   


I will start.   
  
One of my favorite games ever is Dwarf Fortress.   
But even with the new UI and graphics i still strugle, and cant stop thinking how DF would be amazing if it was coded in a game in the style of Minecraft or "Lay of the Land".  

So this is my commission:  
A minecraft style Dwarf fortress fantasy adventure game with voxels and a proceduraly generated map that can be changed, dug, and build upon.   
With the diging, the super in depth simulation, civilizations, wars, culture, deep NPCs, very deep crafting, etc. 

Obviously the game would be very heavy if it needed to render every single creature in the world.   
so we problably need to work in chunks of the map.   
It would also be great if the AI dev could add the "circus surprise" if you know what i mean.

comments.author: coyote1942
comments.body:
A kind of 2d top down version of what star citizen is trying to be.  
Fully detailed interactive ship interiors with all the systems. Seamless ship to ship and ship to station combat. Ship to planet surface could have a cut scene.   
Detailed multiple star systems but not infinite. Simulated economy, dynamic procedural missions.  
Life sim and survival elements like rim world, need to eat a little maybe for buffs, bathing, sleep. Life sim elements simulated npc for ship crew, romance make it nsfw because why not.

replies.author: RamonDozol
replies.body:
So, depth over graphics? 

Also, why not mix the good from both Star citizen and No man's sky?  
Proceduraly generated terrains, billions of planets with diferent procedural rocks, plants, animals, aliens and ships.   
Procedural tech, weapons, items. For this we would need characters that are simulated in depth, and can be affected in many ways. Similarly with magic.   
for example, if you have a speed value, you can add medicine, boots, mechs,  that increases it, or alow you to walk of metal (magnetic boots) or levitate above ground, or fly, or just move in 0G ( space). 

Many items become pre requisites to even do some stuff.   
you need a helmet to go into space or underwater, or to planets/moons that dont have the atmospheric needs your race requires.   
Maybe you need an exoskeleton to be able to walk in high gravity places.   
maybe you can still explore them remotely via drones, or robots of all kinds of shapes, and uses.   
A flying drone would require atmo, a wheeled one would require relatively clean terrain. 

as for weapons, we could come up with diferent "kinds" like energy ( beams, eletricity, light, radiation, etc) kinetic ( shoots objects fast), Biological ( regenerative ammo overtime, but can die and requires something to live.), Chemical ( exlosives, gases, acids, bases. etc) 

The armor/shield could have diferent values of defense for each "damage style".   
energy shield deflects energy best, but might not affect bio or chemical at all.   
Phisical shields deflect kinetic, bio and chemical, being weak to energy that slowly heats it up, until everyone inside is cooked.   
Chemical and bio defenses are problably weak to specific kinetic AND energy of specific kinds.   
A beetle sheel will resist blunt knetic force up until a certain limit, but piercing rounds go right through. A chemical coating is VERY strong, but weaknens quickly once ruptured by a cut or burned hole.

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body:
The way to do this is by first creating custom engine and figuring out method to make those all run optimized.

I have created some draft on the concept but put it on backburner since the scale is huge.

The key is by figuring out first solution for those problem, i do this by working from existing solution from other custom engine.

This part alone already ton of work as we dont have acess to source 

Than from there fusing the solution polosihing it so it become one engine.

Only after this can you start building the game.

comments.author: 12OffIntx
comments.body:
Here is an idea I had that I even have a partial design document and a production plan for from discussing with either Astra or Fable. Assuming this recent obsession of mine even persists, I have two other projects that are going to take a few months so I would love to see someone else's take on it, if it is even interesting.

I guess its sort of Oregon Trail + Fantasy RTS + Roguelite? Game is about moving a caravan through a hostile fantasy wilderness. Six possible biomes, each game is ten stops each in three different maps/biomes. Biomes have unique enemy sets as well as environmental challenges. Branching paths ala things like slay the spire with a boss at the tenth. Only the path option immediately in front of you is visible until you've used meta-upgrades to improve scouting.

Each stop is either something like a merchant or rest or is an RTS battle lasting 3 minutes - defense, attack, protect gatherers, etc. Crafting from the gathering and from killing attackers can be used to upgrade your guards, the caravan, etc. during the run. Meta progression unlocks crafting recipes and new classes and abilities permanently for your caravan guards as well as improvements to the caravan itself.

That's about as far as I got with the idea. Its something I would be interested in playing and seems very doable.
